name: Sagitta
introduction: is the Arrow, the third-smallest constellation, a little arrow flying through the Milky Way between Aquila and Vulpecula. It is best seen on northern summer evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Sagitta contains the globular cluster M71, which was long thought to be an open cluster because its stars are relatively young and loosely packed.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Gamma Sagittae](hip:98337), the arrow’s tip, is a red giant. [Delta Sagittae](hip:97365) is a red giant with a hot companion, and [Sham](hip:96757) a yellow giant.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: WR 124, a Wolf–Rayet star racing through space, is surrounded by clumps of gas and dust it has shed; in 2023 the James Webb Space Telescope imaged them in striking detail.
